worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=\pi .$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡t+4{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot 2\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =8\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity ${sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t=1,$ we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =8\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =8\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
html:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated 2π radians about the y-axis using the formula

S=∫2πxds.

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

ds=(dxdt)2+(dydt)2dt. Therefore, we will use

S=2π∫t1t2x(dxdt)2+(dydt)2dt.

We are told that the limits of integration are from t1=0 to t2=π.

Computing the derivatives, we get

dxdt=ddt(2sin⁡t)=2cos⁡tdydt=ddt(2cos⁡t)=−2sin⁡t.

Therefore,

S=2π∫t1t2x(dxdt)2+(dydt)2dt=2π∫0π2sin⁡t(2cos⁡t)2+(−2sin⁡t)2dt=4π∫0πsin⁡t4cos2⁡t+4sin2⁡tdt=4π∫0πsin⁡t4(sin2⁡t+cos2⁡t)dt=4π∫0πsin⁡t⋅2⋅sin2⁡t+cos2⁡tdt=8π∫0πsin⁡tsin2⁡t+cos2⁡tdt.

Now, using the identity sin2⁡t+cos2⁡t=1, we can rewrite our integral as follows:

S=8π∫0πsin⁡tsin2⁡t+cos2⁡tdt=8π∫0πsin⁡tdt.
